content: There are two distinct types of talk pages. The first type, standard talk pages, is specifically used for discussions related to an article. The second type, user talk pages, is designed for communication between users or for leaving messages for other users. Every page, except those in the Special: namespace, has an associated talk page. If no discussion exists for a page, the link to its talk page will appear red. However, you can still initiate a discussion on the page, becoming the first person to do so. To access a talk page, look for a link labeled Talk, Discussion, or Discuss this page. These links are typically located either at the top of the page or on the left-hand side near the Edit this page option. A talk page is identified by the prefix Talk: added to the beginning of the main page's title. If the main page has a prefix, the Talk prefix is added after it. For instance, a talk page associated with the main article namespace will simply have the prefix Talk:, while a talk page linked to the user namespace will have the prefix User talk:. For example, this article is in the Help: namespace, so its talk page is titled Help talk: Talk page. The Main Page, being in the main namespace (as it has no prefix), has its talk page titled Talk: Main Page. If someone edits your user talk page, an alert stating You have new messages will automatically appear on all pages you view until you visit your user talk page. When using talk pages, it is important to sign your contributions. This can be done by typing three tildes (~~~) to display your username or four tildes (~~~~) to include your username along with a timestamp (e.g., Username 19:36, 10 January 2006 (UTC)). When discussing the name of a page or considering merging it with another page, always mention the current page name. This is because references to this page name would no longer make sense after renaming (moving) the page. If you are referring to the talk page itself, use the term this talk page. The Post a comment feature allows you to conveniently append a section with a section header that matches the edit summary, which only needs to be typed once. However, the practice of spamming, which involves posting similar messages to multiple users' talk pages, often to solicit a specific action, is discouraged. Proper formatting is essential for maintaining readable talk pages, as the wiki software platform provides a wide range of formatting styles. The depth of a message is determined by the number of colons (':') placed in front of it. Each colon represents a tab and is commonly used in discussions on user and article talk pages. When replying to a statement, you should add one colon to the number of colons used in the statement being replied to. This style of conversation improves readability and organization.
